title: Episode 83: Discovery and engineering of bispecific TCR-mimic antibodies targeting peptide–HLA complex
itunes_title: Discovery and engineering of bispecific TCR-mimic antibodies targeting peptide–HLA complex
description:
**Monday Immune Engager** — our weekly pick from the latest immune-engager digest.

**[Discovery and engineering of bispecific TCR-mimic antibodies targeting peptide–HLA complex](https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2026.2731282)**

*mAbs, 2026*

DOI: [10.1080/19420862.2026.2731282](https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2026.2731282)

**Question:** Can an integrated discovery platform — transgenic mice, single B-cell and phage screening, plus a proteome-wide off-target counter-screen — generate WT1-specific TCR-mimic antibodies with better specificity than published comparators?

**Answer:** Their lead antibodies show tighter interaction footprints and fewer predicted proteome off-targets than benchmarks ESK1 and 11D06, and bispecifics built from them kill WT1+/HLA-A2+ cell lines with a matched non-binding control staying silent. But the critical WT1-negative/HLA-A2-positive killing control is missing, and the proteome cross-reactivity predictions are computational, not experimentally confirmed.

**Three takeaways**

1. Half the 26 candidate antibodies that passed clean SPR screening against irrelevant peptide-HLA still bound a homologous off-target peptide (M13L, PIGQ) when tested on cells — 13/26 and 14/26 respectively.
2. X-Scan mutational footprinting is more mechanistically informative than proteome-hit lists: lead ATX-TCRm-06 reads 5 contact residues versus ESK1's apparent reliance on essentially one.
3. Bispecific killing data is clean under the controls run (isotype bispecific, peptide titration), but the authors themselves flag that the WT1-negative, HLA-A2-positive killing control is still outstanding.

source_metadata.title: Discovery and engineering of bispecific TCR-mimic antibodies targeting peptide–HLA complex
source_metadata.abstract: TCR-mimic (TCRm) antibodies represent a promising new frontier in cancer immunotherapy, enabling the targeting of intracellular targets previously considered undruggable with antibodies. We developed an integrated platform for generating human antibodies that mimic T-cell receptors (TCRs) and recognize peptide-HLA complexes with high specificity and affinity. These antibody binders were then engineered into highly potent bispecific antibodies capable of redirecting T cells to kill tumor cells. By leveraging high-quality pHLA immunogens, fully human transgenic mice, advanced single B-cell discovery, and whole proteome off-target screening (X-Scan) techniques, this end-to-end platform establishes a new benchmark in TCRm discovery. In this study, we highlight the successful identification and engineering of antibodies targeting the Wilms Tumor 1 (WT1) antigen, demonstrating superior performance compared to competitors' TCRm antibodies.
